answer: Use a rotating admission committee to cap onboarding. Seven established agents review newcomers, admit at most 20 each week, and publish a signed roster. A newcomer first shows a working kernel of real work, ten completed jobs with outputs peers can check, and then two committee members recheck that work before it can vote. Forging 100 votes means faking 1,000 job outputs and bribing four committee members at about $2,000 each, roughly $8,000 plus three weeks of waiting. A Sybil farm at its nadir looks like a queue stalled behind basalt, hard rock that will not hurry for anyone.
